Q: User consent to apps accessing company data on their behalf is not allowed A:

It isn't completely clear what logic is used in the Portal to determine what option is checked, however here is an estimation, you can get the User consent settings by querying Get authorizationPolicy and inspecting the permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned property from defaultUserRolePermissions:

Connect-MgGraph -Scopes Policy.Read.All

$uri = 'v1.0/policies/authorizationPolicy?$select=defaultUserRolePermissions'
$req = Invoke-MgGraphRequest GET $uri
$req.defaultUserRolePermissions.permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned

Note in the details of defaultUserRolePermissions:

Indicates if user consent to apps is allowed, and if it is, which permission to grant consent and which app consent policy (permissionGrantPolicy) govern the permission for users to grant consent. Value should be in the format managePermissionGrantsForSelf.{id}, where {id} is the id of a built-in or custom app consent policy. An empty list indicates user consent to apps is disabled.

Then checking the Built-in consent policies there is a warning that says:

microsoft-user-default-recommended and microsoft-user-default-allow-consent-apps are a Microsoft managed policies. The conditions included in the policies are automatically updated based on Microsoft's latest security recommendations for end-user consent.

So my estimation is:

$userConsentSettings = $req.defaultUserRolePermissions.permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned
if ($userConsentSettings.Length -eq 0) {
    # this means that the first option is checked
}
elseif ($userConsentSettings -match '\.microsoft-user-default-(?:recommended|allow-consent-apps)') {
    # this means that the last option is checked 
}
else {
    # the middle option is checked
}

In my case, I have the middle option checked and if I inspect the array of permissionGrantPoliciesAssigned I have ManagePermissionGrantsForSelf.microsoft-user-default-low which according to the docs is:

  • microsoft-user-default-low: All low risk permissions consentable by member type users by default.

Q: What does this passage from CLRS mean? A:

I interpreted it as follows.

Let $f \in O(g)$, where $g$ is the function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ such that $g(n) = n$ for any $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
Then, $\sum_{i = 1}^{n} O(i)$ is the real number $\sum_{i = 1}^{n} f(i)$ for such a function $f$.

Q: How do I disable *automatic* autocomplete in VS Code? A:

VS Code accepts autocomplete suggestions when certain "commit characters" are typed (such as (, ., ;, etc.).

To prevent "(" from automatically accepting a suggestion while still allowing Tab to accept suggestions:

Open Settings (JSON):

Ctrl + Shift + P

Preferences: Open Settings (JSON)

Add this line to your settings.json:

{
  "editor.acceptSuggestionOnCommitCharacter": false
}

This disables accepting suggestions when typing characters like "(", while Tab or Enter can still be used to accept suggestions manually.

Q: How to return row where items are grouped by Id and related reference fields? A:

We can consider this task as follows:

  • find the root nodes of the tree that have child nodes
  • and also find the next node in the tree.

Nodes linked by rule Child.Ref1 = LEFT(parent.Ref2, LEN(Child.Ref1))

Recursive query

WITH r AS(
     SELECT 0 as lvl,t.GroupId,t.ItemId,t.Ref1,t.Ref2
     FROM @test t
     WHERE ref1 is null  -- root node
       AND exists (      -- node have child node
           SELECT 1 from @test t2 
           WHERE t2.GroupId=t.GroupId 
                 AND t2.ref1=left(t.ref2,len(t2.ref1))
            )
     UNION ALL
     SELECT lvl+1 as lvl,r.GroupId,t.ItemId,t.Ref1,t.Ref2
     FROM r INNER JOIN @test t ON r.GroupId=t.GroupId 
       AND t.Ref1 = left(r.Ref2, len(t.Ref1))
       AND lvl<1 -- limit number of childs {0,1}
   )
SELECT * FROM r ORDER BY GroupId,ItemId;

Example

Q: How do I get the external IP of a socket in Python? A:

ifconfig.me

I would like to add a really nice site that I use (and it's shorter than most of mentioned here). Using a browser the site shows you your IP, user agent and bunch of headers and also has great command line interface (user agent curl or python-requests).

For example these will print your public IP address:

import requests

print(requests.get("https://ifconfig.me").text)

curl ifconfig.me

Showcase of some useful endpoints:

  • https://ifconfig.me/ip
  • https://ifconfig.me/ua
  • https://ifconfig.me/all.json

Q: pivot_longer() with several sets of columns A:

The regex pattern you need requires two capture groups (): one for the pathogen column names, and one for the median|mad values:

library(tidyr)

data_example |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -drug_name,
    names_to = c("pathogen", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(pathogen\\d+)_(median|mad)_molar"
  )
# A tibble: 4 × 4
#   drug_name pathogen  median   mad
#   <chr>     <chr>      <dbl> <dbl>
# 1 drug1     pathogen1      1  0.5 
# 2 drug1     pathogen2      2  0.25
# 3 drug2     pathogen1      4  2   
# 4 drug2     pathogen2      8  1

The regex works like this:

  • from the start of the column name strings ^
  • (pathogen\\d+) captures the literal string "pathogen" only if it is followed by one or more digits \\d+
  • _(median|mad)_molar captures any columns that have either the literal "median" or "mad" if they fall between the literals "_" and "_molar"

The elements in the names_to = parameter correspond, in order, to each capture group. ".value" allows you to pivot one column for each unique string found in the second capture group. In your case, values associated with column names containing "median" or "mad" get their own column.

Q: Why does /Account/Login briefly render then disappear in a .NET 10 Blazor Web App using InteractiveServer and ASP.NET Identity? A:

Okay found a workaround by not specifying the render mode in my app.razor and just specifying on the pages where I need interactivity mode to be interactiveserver.

Q: Django 3.0.5 with mod_wsgi: AttributeError: 'HttpResponse' object has no attribute '_resource_closers' A:

In my case, the error object has no attribute '_resource_closers' was raised due to problems in the middleware. When settings.DEBUG = True this middleware was returning a modified response, settings.DEBUG = False it was not returning anything at all.
